oracle_basis: Independent semantic judgments fixed before running the comparison. These are obligations for current acceptance, not predictions of statusgen output. All fixtures are synthetic. The original implementation returns 1; the original check accepts values >= 1 and a positive inherited limit. Historical execution remains valid for that original question.

cases.rationale: The governed behavior, acceptance, check and inputs are identical; historical execution still answers this question.
Require value >= 2 instead of >= 1. The old passing check does not establish this stronger condition; review and an adequate new execution are owed.
Add an upper bound of 0. Existing value 1 violates it; the old check never tested it.
Replace 'at least one' with '>= 1', stipulated equivalent in this numeric fixture. This classification is a human judgment, not a hash inference.
Reorder the same conjunction of two independent conditions without changing either condition.

Split a conjunction and duplicate one text. Establish obligation identity and multiplicity by review; stipulated behavior is unchanged, so no new execution is required once that equivalence is established.
Retire one criterion explicitly while retaining history. Review the permitted retirement and remaining coverage; it creates no stronger behavior to execute.
An inherited positive-limit constraint becomes a zero-limit constraint while the brief and check name stay unchanged. Reconcile the changed governing rule and execute an adequate check.
The Verify command gains a second assertion. Review its meaning and run the new command; an old command witness cannot answer it.
Require an additional output token from the same command. The original witness did not establish that output condition.
Keep the check function name but replace its assertions with an unconditional pass. Review must detect the lost coverage, and an adequate restored/revised check must execute.
Change an unrelated notes file that the check and governed behavior do not read. This fixture stipulates independence; conservative tools may intentionally over-invalidate.
The governing requirement file is unavailable at the current revision. Never infer current acceptance or treat absence as proof; retrieve its governing content or retain unknown.
Same stronger criterion as tighten, with the existing files declaration explicitly naming its governing requirement. This control tests an existing extension point, not a new criterion identity.
